draft_elevation.note: RECONSTRUCTED by the draft rules, family row '(default)' overlaid with the frontage row: The Tucker/Smith house (Van Osdel, 1876), Byron L. Smith's in 1904: the register's 'mansard/dormers, tall stacks' over the 3S.B. brick body and the sheet's round bay at the 22nd Street corner as a round tower. ONE ROOF STATE, as the register requires: its towers are drawn FLAT-TOPPED AND CRESTED, the house's first state (the pre-1881 stereo, under Tucker's name), because the conical spires are dated only by a 1928 photograph and nothing puts them on the house by 1904; a dated view showing spires by July 1904 replaces this state (T-1928, T-1929). The three-storey building at the alley corner is no one's stable: its 1911 use (CATERER) is not carried back, and it stands as an outbuilding. Heights are the rules' starting values inside RECONSTRUCTION-RULES.md's ranges; bays, entrance side, chimneys and dormers are counts the family rules choose, and the seed 3369658031 only tints the fabric inside +-6 %. Liberty L-draft-prairie-20-22-west-2351.

research_note: A DISTRICT DRAFT (T-2351, the owner's district pass of 2026-10-08): a serviceable first model, complete from the street, the walks, the alley and the air, that T-1928, T-1929 refine in place under this same id. Written by tools/draft_prairie_1904.py from the sheet 35 trace (s35fp-2140-b1), the T-1842 census (s35-2140-front, s35-2140-wing, s35-2140-walls) and the T-1837 register row frontage-35-071 (Tucker/Smith polychrome corner mansion); every height, roof, opening and feature is the draft rules' reconstruction (data/components/prairie_1904/draft_prairie_1904.json; liberty L-draft-prairie-20-22-west-2351).
